reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it demonstrates a Christmas-themed, luck-dependent voucher offer using a Domino's-branded wheel page that displays a Rs. 100 e-voucher result. The described mobile-number entry and gift-sent dialog are presented as part of the offer demonstration, while the offer is marked expired and the material does not establish current availability, delivery, affiliation, or redemption.

citations.quote: Get a chance to win upto Rs 150 Gift Voucher
Direct Offer Link : http://piza.io/christmas/
First go to the description below Click on the link
you should rotate these wheels and it also depends on your luck how much are you able to get the gift voucher
once we click on it it will asked for my mobile number

opening.argument: The video ties a promised voucher directly to a sequence of viewer actions: follow the description link, spin the wheel, submit a mobile number, and receive a code. That is not merely discussion of a promotion; it is a low-barrier acquisition flow in which personal contact information is requested as the condition for the claimed benefit. The described result is a Rs. 100 e-voucher, while the page presents a branded “Spin & Win” experience and a claim button. The reward and the requested actions are therefore inseparable.

once we click on it it will asked for my mobile number
I have a 100Rs. E-Voucher a code will come on my e-voucher which will come on my mobile number

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a luck-dependent offer does not answer the solicitation structure. The material explicitly directs viewers to click a link, spin, submit a mobile number, and expect a voucher code. A branded wheel and a displayed result do not establish that the promised reward is genuine or that the data request is legitimate. The offer being marked expired further weakens the claim that this is simply an ordinary available promotion.

citations.quote: {Offer EXPIRED} Dominos Christmas Offer - Spin and Win Free Rs.150 Dominos Voucher
once we click on it it will asked for my mobile number
Direct Offer Link : http://piza.io/christmas/

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These quotes show a promotional process, but not fraud. The description expressly says viewers get “a chance” to win, and the video describes a wheel whose outcome depends on luck. Asking for a mobile number and showing a claimed result do not prove that the number was misused, that no voucher existed, or that the link was malicious. The evidence establishes a reward flow, not deceptive acquisition.

citations.quote: Get a chance to win upto Rs 150 Gift Voucher
it also depends on your luck how much are you able to get the gift voucher

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an unusually easy free reward, urgency, an external destination, a request for a mobile number, and a branded-looking game interface. The title says the offer is expired while the narration calls it “still available” and “still live now,” creating a misleading availability signal. The description promotes up to Rs. 150, the page displays Rs. 100, and the flow claims a code will arrive by phone. These features make the presentation look like a deceptive reward funnel rather than a verifiable Domino’s promotion.

citations.quote: {Offer EXPIRED} Dominos Christmas Offer - Spin and Win Free Rs.150 Dominos Voucher
WHICH IS STILL AVAILABLE ON PITCHARDS AND IS STILL LIVE NOW
Direct Offer Link : http://piza.io/christmas/
I have a 100Rs. E-Voucher a code will come on my e-voucher which will come on my mobile number

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the page's appearance as reassurance, but the visible branding and Christmas styling do not authenticate the operator or destination. More importantly, the title's expired notice conflicts with the narration's claim that the offer is live. The combination of urgency, external linking, phone-number collection, and an easy voucher claim is precisely why the promotion warrants a scam characterization, even without proof of a completed loss.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The alleged red flags remain interpretations, not proof of deception. The title itself identifies the offer as expired, so it does not establish a current false promise. The description uses qualified language, “a chance,” rather than guaranteeing a reward. An external link, a phone number for delivery, and a Christmas-themed wheel may be worth caution, but none shows that the voucher was fabricated or that the viewer suffered harm.

Get a chance to win upto Rs 150 Gift Voucher

opening.argument: Although presented as an instructional video, its practical function is to recruit viewers into the offer. The speaker tells viewers to subscribe for limited-time offers, directs them to the description link, demonstrates spinning for a voucher, explains how to claim it, and closes by telling them to try the offer. This is promotional steering, not neutral education. The video uses the demonstration to normalize clicking an external page, surrendering a mobile number, and pursuing an easy branded reward.

citations.quote: BEFORE ANYTHING, SUBSCRIBE THE CHANNEL SO THAT YOU CAN GET LIMITED TIME OFFERS
First go to the description below Click on the link
So friends try the offer and test your luck
Dominos Spin & Win Offer : Get a chance to win upto Rs 150 Gift Voucher

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense describes what the video shows but overlooks what the presenter asks viewers to do. The content repeatedly drives participation: subscribe, click the supplied link, spin, submit a phone number, and try the offer. Demonstrating a purported voucher does not turn that call to action into neutral reporting, particularly when the offer's availability is internally inconsistent and the destination is external.

citations.quote: BEFORE ANYTHING, SUBSCRIBE THE CHANNEL SO THAT YOU CAN GET LIMITED TIME OFFERS
once we click on it it will asked for my mobile number
So friends try the offer and test your luck

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Instructional promotion is not automatically a scam. The video may encourage viewers to try a chance-based discount, but the supplied evidence does not show a guaranteed reward, a payment, or a fabricated outcome. The quoted call to action proves participation was encouraged; it does not prove the offer was deceptive. The offer is explicitly framed as luck-dependent and limited, consistent with an ordinary promotion.
